There's no likelihood of snow this winter.

vocabulary.meaning_en: for as long as we can imagine now
vocabulary.example: Prices will stay high for the foreseeable future.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the money you are paid for your job, usually monthly
vocabulary.example: He asked for a higher salary.

vocabulary.meaning_ar: يؤجّل قبول دعوة إلى وقت لاحق
vocabulary.example: I can't come tonight. Can I take a rain check?
There's a good chance I'll be there.
The chances of winning are pretty slim.
The new building got the green light.

vocabulary.meaning_en: showing that something bad will happen
leave a course or school before finishing

vocabulary.example: The weather is bound to improve.

fine_lines.title: How likely? From impossible to certain
words: It's bound to / There's no doubt
fine_lines.explanation_ar: There's absolutely no way / no likelihood = مستحيل تقريبًا. It's unlikely = مستبعد. There's a good chance / The chances are / As likely as not = محتمل جدًا. It seems inevitable / is bound to / There's no doubt = شبه مؤكد.
fine_lines.explanation_en: No way / no likelihood = almost impossible. Unlikely = probably not. A good chance / the chances are / as likely as not = probably yes. Inevitable / bound to / no doubt = almost certain.

examples.sentence: There's absolutely no way he'll agree.

examples.word: It's bound to / There's no doubt
examples.sentence: The weather is bound to improve next week.

fine_lines.title: Formal vs neutral/informal prediction phrases
fine_lines.explanation_ar: There's no likelihood of وAs likely as not أكثر رسمية. It's unlikely that محايدة. There's a good chance that غير رسمية/محايدة.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "There's no likelihood of" and "As likely as not" are more formal. "It's unlikely that" is neutral. "There's a good chance that" is neutral or informal.

examples.sentence: There's no likelihood of prices coming down soon.
There's a good chance that I'll join you on Saturday.

expressions.meaning_en: A formal way to say something won't happen.
expressions.example: There's no likelihood of snow this winter.

expressions.meaning_en: A neutral way to say something probably won't happen.
expressions.example: It's unlikely that I'll be able to come to the dinner.

expressions.meaning_en: A strong way to say something won't happen.
expressions.example: There's absolutely no way the boss will agree to that.

expressions.meaning_en: A formal way to say something will probably happen.
expressions.example: As likely as not, he'll call and cancel.
There's a good chance I'll have to travel for work next month.
The chances are that they'll get planning permission.

expressions.meaning_en: Says something is not very likely.
expressions.example: Will we win? The chances are pretty slim.

expressions.meaning_en: Says something is almost certain to happen.
expressions.example: It seems inevitable that prices will go up.
The weather is bound to improve next week.

expressions.phrase: There's no doubt (in my mind) that ...
expressions.example: There's no doubt in my mind that it's the right decision.

expressions.phrase: Can I take a rain check?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل يمكن أن نؤجّل ذلك لوقت آخر؟
expressions.meaning_en: Politely says no to an invitation for now.
expressions.example: I'm busy on Friday. Can I take a rain check?

expressions.phrase: I'll let you know for definite.
expressions.example: I'll probably come, but I'll let you know for definite on Thursday.

grammar.title: Prediction phrases + that-clause / of + noun / to + verb
grammar.explanation_ar: بعض العبارات يأتي بعدها that + جملة (It's unlikely that..., There's a good chance that..., The chances are that...). بعضها يأتي بعده of + اسم أو ing (There's no likelihood of snow). وbound to يأتي بعدها الفعل الأساسي.
grammar.explanation_en: Some phrases take "that + clause" (It's unlikely that..., There's a good chance that...). Some take "of + noun / -ing" (There's no likelihood of snow). "Bound to" takes the base verb.
examples: There's no likelihood of prices coming down.
The weather is bound to improve.

grammar.title: will / going to for predictions
grammar.explanation_ar: بعد عبارات التنبؤ نستخدم غالبًا will أو going to للحديث عن المستقبل.
grammar.explanation_en: After prediction phrases we often use "will" or "going to" for the future.
examples: There's a good chance I'll be there.
It's unlikely that he's going to win.
There's no doubt that prices will rise.

questions.question: Which phrase means something is almost CERTAIN?
There's no likelihood ___ snow this winter.
The weather is bound ___ next week.
"As likely as not, he'll cancel" means:
questions.explanation_ar: As likely as not = على الأرجح.

questions.question: Which is the strongest way to say something WON'T happen?
questions.explanation_ar: There's absolutely no way أقوى عبارة للنفي.
questions.explanation_en: "There's absolutely no way" is the strongest.

questions.question: "Can I take a rain check?" means:
choices: Can we do it another time?
questions.explanation_ar: take a rain check = تأجيل الدعوة لوقت لاحق.
questions.explanation_en: It means "can we do it another time?"

questions.question: There's a good chance ___ I'll be there on Saturday.
questions.explanation_ar: There's a good chance that + جملة.
questions.explanation_en: There's a good chance that + clause.

questions.question: "The project got the green light" means:
choices: It was given permission to start.
questions.explanation_ar: get the green light = يحصل على الموافقة.
questions.explanation_en: It means it was allowed to start.
